assessment_summary: I validated the QuattroMap installation against the guide's Develop section (npm install → npm start on http://localhost:8080/ → npm run build to dist/). Inspection steps: (1) Confirmed runtime prerequisites (Node 20.20.2, npm 10.8.2) and the repo state (clean git tree at commit 24041c0, matching the summary; dist/ and node_modules are gitignored). (2) Verified dependency completeness: all 17 direct dependencies from package.json exist in /workspace/node_modules. (3) Verified the build artifact: /workspace/dist/ contains exactly the outputs defined by webpack.config.js's CopyPlugin and LicensePlugin (index.html, bundle.js, img/, vendor/maplibre/*.mjs, oss-licenses.json); the production bundle embeds src/config.json values (center 6.391263, configured layers), and src/config.json is valid JSON with center/zoom/map_1..map_4 and 120 layer definitions matching the guide's configuration schema. (4) Functional check of the dev server: I started `npm start` (the guide's documented startup); webpack 5.110.3 compiled with 5 warnings and no errors; I then fetched the app over HTTP on port 8080 — index.html (200, title 'QuattroMap', contains the four map_1..map_4 containers the JS initializes), bundle.js (200), and both maplibre worker/shared modules (200). (5) Functional check of the production build: served /workspace/dist/ with a plain static HTTP server; index.html, bundle.js, and image assets all returned 200 with expected sizes and content. (6) Restored the environment: stopped the webpack dev server and static server by PID, verified no node/webpack processes and no listening ports remained. Limitations: no browser is available in the container, so I could not visually render the UI or confirm live WMS tile loading from external services (wms.nrw.de); runtime rendering was inferred from a clean compile, all assets serving correctly, and the app's DOM structure. `npm run deploy` (gh-pages publishing) was not exercised, but it is an optional publishing convenience, not a local-installation requirement, and the dist/ it would publish is present and valid. Based on the objective evidence that the app builds, compiles, and serves in both dev and static modes per the guide, the installation is complete and operational.
